Boulet — de son vrai nom Gilles Roussel: Boulet — real name Gilles Roussel — is a major figure of French-language comics. Discovered by the creator of Titeuf, he took off in the mid-2000s with the slice-of-life strips on his blog, then his albums and illustrations. Ten years ago he launched his Twitch channel. And what he does there is, at first glance, a hard sell: he draws. Live. For hours.
Et pourtant, ça fonctionne. Parce que Bo: And yet, it works. Because BouletCorp isn't a tutorial or a masterclass — it's an open studio. Boulet draws, talks, chats with his cat, shares his doubts, his thoughts on creation, society, his moods, the fatigue of creating. You watch a drawing come to life, line by line, while chatting with the artist.
Boulet dessine de tête, sans croquis pré: Boulet draws from memory, with no preliminary sketch. Straight to the final drawing on the page. That's exceptional — almost every professional goes through a sketch. Boulet joins a very rare lineage: Cabu, Moebius, Enki Bilal, Hugo Pratt, Kim Jung Gi. On Twitch, it's a genuine public high-wire act.
Auto-dérision, blagues geek, références: Self-deprecation, geek jokes, nerd references, meta humour, unlikely digressions. The ability to turn a serious thought into a punchline in half a second. And sometimes, when you can feel the fatigue creeping in, it gets even funnier.
Pas de sur-excitation permanente. Pas de: No constant over-excitement. No artificial staging. No "like, subscribe, hit the bell". A long, calm, intelligent time, watching someone practise their passion honestly. For anyone who loves drawing or creating, it's almost therapeutic.
BouletCorp, ce n'est pas juste une chaîn: BouletCorp isn't just a Twitch drawing channel. It's a live creative diary — funny, clear-eyed, sometimes acid or melancholy, often brilliant. You come to learn, to relax, or just to watch someone do what they love… while wondering out loud why he still does it after all these years.
Ce qui ressort le plus : Boulet ne sacra: What stands out most: Boulet never sanctifies drawing. No claimed magic gift, no staging of genius. Desire, curiosity, discipline. And the moments of hesitation, of being stuck, of redrawing the same element three times are visible — which, for anyone who loves drawing or would like to start, is precious and reassuring.
